references.text: Agur's words ask: "Who has ascended to heaven and come down again?" ([ref:Prov 30:4|Proverbs 30:4]). This question points prophetically forward to Jesus as the only one who has ascended to heaven and come down from there, which John 3:13 provides the answer to.

Moses says that no one has ascended to heaven to bring God's word down ([ref:Deut 30:12|Deuteronomy 30:12]). Jesus claims in John 3:13 that he himself is the one who has come down from heaven and thus has authority to reveal God's will.

"No one has ever seen God, but the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known" ([ref:John 1:18|John 1:18]). Both verses emphasize that Jesus is the only one with direct access to heaven and can reveal God's reality to humanity.

Jesus speaks of the disciples seeing heaven opened and God's angels ascending and descending over the Son of Man ([ref:John 1:51|John 1:51]). The Son of Man is the connection between heaven and earth, which is confirmed in John 3:13.
Jesus says: "For I have come down from heaven" ([ref:John 6:38|John 6:38]). This is a direct parallel to John 3:13 where Jesus describes himself as the one who descended from heaven.

Jesus asks the disciples what they would say if they saw the Son of Man ascending to where he was before ([ref:John 6:62|John 6:62]). The verse confirms that the Son of Man has his origin in heaven and will return there, in agreement with John 3:13.

Paul writes that Christ first descended to the lowest parts of the earth and then ascended above all heavens ([ref:Eph 4:9-10|Ephesians 4:9-10]). This reflects the same pattern as in John 3:13: descent from heaven and ascent back.

Daniel sees in a vision "one like a son of man" coming with the clouds of heaven ([ref:Dani 7:13|Daniel 7:13]). The expression "Son of Man" in John 3:13 links Jesus to this heavenly figure in Daniel's prophecy.

"He who comes from above is over all" ([ref:John 3:31|John 3:31]). The verse expands on the theme from John 3:13 regarding Jesus' heavenly origin and his unique authority as the one who has come down from heaven.

Jesus says: "I came out from the Father and have come into the world. I am leaving the world again and going to the Father" ([ref:John 16:28|John 16:28]). This summarizes the movement described in John 3:13: the descent from heaven and the coming ascension.
